Definition: a primary verb; to swell out, i.e. be full:--be full.
BiblicalUsage: I take gémō to mean be full, nothing more and nothing less. It occurs 11 times, and Matthew and Luke show it doing ordinary work in ordinary sentences. The Bible uses plain words plainly, and this is one of them.
TheologicalSignificance: gémō matters to me because God speaks plainly, and plain words carry real weight. My position is that Scripture does not hide its meaning from honest readers.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
